packages.label: קְדֻשַּׁת הַבְּרִית וּמִילָה
packages.label_en: Holiness of the Covenant and Circumcision
packages.reason: All four nodes are different expressions of the same essential reality: the holiness of the covenant of circumcision as embodied by Joseph the Tzaddik. מ"ל is explicitly called 'בחינת מילה'; קדשת הברית is called 'בחינת מילה'; and יוסף is called 'בחינת קדשת הברית, בחינת מילה כנודע'. They form a chain: יוסף — קדשת הברית — מילה — מ"ל, all four being aspects of sexual purity and the holy covenant. The Torah explicitly identifies מ"ל as the component within חשמ"ל that represents מילה, i.e., the nullification of the ערלה. This is the positive pole of the teaching's central axis.

packages.label: חַשְׁמַ"ל וְנֹגַהּ
packages.label_en: Chashmal and Nogah — The Intermediate Domain
packages.reason: Both nodes represent the threshold domain between holiness and impurity — the fourth layer that can be absorbed into kedusha or fall into klipa. The Torah identifies נגה as the fourth klipa (corresponding to the fourth year fruit, revi'i) situated between the three impure klipot and kedusha, and states 'והוא בחינות חשמ"ל, כי לפעמים נכלכלת במ"ל אורות'. Nogah IS chashmal — the domain that sometimes contains lights of מ"ל (kedusha) and sometimes falls into the klipot. This is the neutral, oscillating domain whose essential nature is ambiguity and potential. The three years of ערלה = three impure klipot; the fourth year (revi'i/nogah) = chashmal = the borderline that can go either way.
merge_notes: The source text (line 16) contains explicit bechina language linking שתיקה to this component: 'זאת השתיקה שהיא בחינת חשמ"ל, זהו בחינת נגה'. This creates a bechina bridge to Package 5 not yet captured in the dataset. The gap analysis (torah_82_additions.json) documents this missing edge. If that edge were added, Package 2 and Package 5 would merge into a single larger component. For now, as separate bechina components, they remain separate packages.

Similarly, the text says 'השתיקה, שהיא בחינת מילה' (line 15), which would bridge Package 2 (via its link to Package 5 through שתיקה=חשמ"ל) to Package 1. These are missing bechina edges documented in additions.

packages.label: שַׁלְהֶבֶת יָהּ
packages.label_en: The Flame of God — Divine Protective Fire
packages.reason: Both nodes are expressions of the divine flame of holy love that repels impurity from attaching to holiness on Shabbat eve. The proof text states: 'ואז יורדים בחינת שלהבת י"ה, ומכוה אותן שלא יאחזו בקדשה, והוא בחינת מים חמין' — the hot water for bathing before Shabbat IS an aspect of the flame of Yah. The essential nature shared by both is: the burning divine love (stronger than death, per Shir HaShirim 8) that protects the boundary of holiness. The text further confirms at line 13 that this same שלהבת י"ה is what the verse 'ואוהביו כצאת השמש בגבורתו' refers to — it is the blazing love of those who practice holy silence.
merge_notes: This component is a 2-node cluster. Its polarity is good (divine). While the eitza chain connects it to the נגה/חשמ"ל domain (the flame acts on nogah to include it in kedusha), its essential NATURE — the divine flame of love stronger than death — is distinct from nogah's nature (the neutral threshold). A bechina-based merge into Package 2 is not warranted: שלהבת י"ה IS the divine fire, not the neutral threshold. They are different aspects of the same teaching structure, connected by eitza (the flame acts on the nogah), not shared essence.

packages.label: עָרְלָה וְשָׁלֹשׁ קְלִפּוֹת
packages.label_en: The Foreskin and the Three Impure Klipot
packages.reason: ערלה and שלש קלפות are explicitly identified as the same essential reality: 'ערלה, שהיא בחינת שלש קלפות הנ"ל'. The foreskin IS the three impure klipot. Both are the source of חרפה (shame/disgrace) — 'כי עיקר החרפות באים מבחינת ערלה, שהיא בחינת שלש קלפות'. This is the evil mirror of Package 1 (קדשת הברית/מילה): just as מילה is the holy covenant, ערלה is its opposite — the domain of impurity, the three klipot (רוח סערה, ענן גדול, אש מתלקחת), and the source of all shame. The circumcision/removal of the foreskin = the removal of the evil klipot = the gathering of all חרפות.

packages.label: חַ"שׁ וּשְׁתִיקָה
packages.reason: ח"ש IS שתיקה — the proof text states this directly: 'ח"ש, הוא שתיקה'. ח"ש is the first component of the word חשמ"ל (ח"ש + מ"ל), and it represents silence. In this Torah, silence is the holy response to insult — the behavior of those who are shamed and do not respond (הנעלבים ואינם עולבים). When practiced from love (מאהבה), this silence is holy, belonging to the domain of kedusha (nogah included in holiness). Both ח"ש and שתיקה share the essential nature of holy silence that transcends speech — the aspect of חשמ"ל that represents the nullification of the power to shame by withholding verbal retaliation. The polarity is good when practiced from love (the context of this Torah).
